outcome_intro: Ask which client users have no verified 911 address, where the main number really rings after hours, or what a departing employee still holds, and get the answer from every client Zoom Phone account at once. The CLI mirrors each account locally for the audits, reads live data for routing and missed calls, and a change made through the MCP server runs only with confirm: true; in the CLI a change is sent at once, and --dry-run is the opt-in preview.

instead_of_say.instead: Clicking through every user, common-area phone and site in each client's Zoom admin portal to check emergency addresses
instead_of_say.say: Which users and phones at Acme have no verified emergency address?

instead_of_say.instead: Opening each auto receptionist and call queue to work out why after-hours calls to the main number go nowhere
instead_of_say.say: Where does a call to our main number ring after hours?

instead_of_say.instead: Hunting through call queues, shared lines, pickup groups, desk phones and numbers to remove a departing employee

pain_points: Every client is a separate Zoom account with its own admin portal, so a question as simple as 'whose 911 address is missing' means logging into each tenant and clicking user by user.
Call routing lives in layers (auto receptionists, IVR keys, call queues, closed-hours rules), so a dead IVR key or an empty queue is found by a customer whose call went nowhere.
Offboarding a user touches queues, shared lines, pickup and monitoring groups, desk phones, numbers and the calling plan, and the portal shows each one on a different page.

outcomes.question: Which users, common areas and sites have a missing or unverified emergency address?
Which phone numbers are unassigned, pending, or still held by an inactive user?
Which desk phones are offline, unassigned or on drifted firmware, by site?
Which external callers missed us this week and have not been called back?
Which IVR keys point at nothing, and which call queues have nobody to answer?
What does this user hold before we remove them?
Run the E911 audit across every client account at once

different_vs_wrappers: This is a Go CLI and MCP server that covers the whole Zoom Phone API (420 tools) and adds audits no single API call answers: E911 coverage, dead routing, number and desk-phone hygiene, unreturned missed calls and an offboarding plan. It keeps one saved profile per client account and runs any read across all of them with fleet. The community Python server [FujitsuPolycom/zoom-phone-mcp](https://github.com/FujitsuPolycom/zoom-phone-mcp) exposes 117 tools for one account.
different_vs_vendor: Zoom ships official MCP servers for Meetings, Team Chat and other products but none for Zoom Phone; this adds Phone, works across every client account you manage, and hands structured JSON to the AI agent you already use.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, so it needs the Zoom MCP server's token-protected HTTP mode hosted over HTTPS. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data. Credentials are saved with the current token in a credentials file readable only by your user, and are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: What Zoom credentials does it need?
faqs.a: A Server-to-Server OAuth app in the Zoom App Marketplace, created in each client account, with the phone admin read scopes your workflow needs (add write scopes only if you want changes). You give the CLI its Account ID, Client ID and Client Secret; save one profile per client with accounts connect.

faqs.q: Will it hit my Zoom rate limits?
faqs.a: Zoom Phone limits are per account and shared by every app. The E911, number and desk-phone audits read the local mirror, so after a sync they make no API calls. Live reads (routing, callbacks, footprint group membership) back off on HTTP 429 and honor Retry-After.

governance_summary: Reads (the audits, routing traces, missed-call lists, footprints, sync and every Zoom Phone GET) change nothing and are safe to allow. Changes to a client account (call forwarding, queue members, settings) should be previewed and then approved: in the CLI a write is sent as soon as it runs and --dry-run is opt-in, while the MCP server runs a write only with confirm: true; deletes, the offboard plan's --apply, phone reboots, firmware and provisioning rules, SMS and emergency-address changes stay human-in-the-loop. Any command that can return a stored secret (device SIP passwords, PINs, activation codes) and any change to roles is credential tier.

safety_tiers.examples: e911 audit, numbers inventory, devices health, callbacks, routing trace, routing audit, footprint, offboard (plan only), sync, search, fleet with a read command, and every list or get that returns no stored secret
users add-call-forward-setting, call-queues members and settings changes, sites and common-areas updates, outbound caller ID and calling rules, client codes on call history
safety_tiers.policy: Preview with --dry-run (opt-in in the CLI; MCP writes always need confirm: true), then a reviewed write

safety_tiers.examples: devices reboot-phone, firmware-update-rules and provision-templates changes, sms post-message, whatsapp post-whats-app-message, emergency-addresses and emergency-services changes

any command that can return a stored secret field (devices get-adevice, common-areas list-activation-codes, users phone-settings, setting-templates get, ported-numbers get-details), roles changes, auth and accounts commands
